news.title: Nicolas Jackson departs Chelsea on permanent transfer
news.body_en: Nicolas Jackson has completed a permanent transfer from Chelsea to Aston Villa. The Senegal international arrived at Stamford Bridge in June 2023 from Spanish club Villarreal. Jackson was part of the Chelsea squads that won the UEFA Conference League and FIFA Club World Cup trophies. He netted 13 goals during that campaign, including one in the Wroclaw showpiece against Real Betis. The 25-year-old featured for the Blues under Xabi Alonso in pre-season, but now heads to Villa Park and brings an end to his time at Stamford Bridge. We thank Nico for his efforts during his time at the club and wish him well for the future.

news.title: Date and kick-off time confirmed for Chelsea vs Leeds United
news.body_en: The date and kick-off time of Chelsea’s Carabao Cup third-round fixture against Leeds United have been confirmed. The Blues will face our old rivals Leeds at Stamford Bridge on Wednesday 9 September. Kick-off will be at 8pm, with the match broadcast live in the UK on Sky Sports Main Event. Full ticket details will be announced in due course but you can already book your hospitality for Chelsea vs Leeds by clicking here.

news.title: FPL 2026/27: Chelsea Gameweek two
news.body_en: Chelsea have teamed up with Fantasy Football Scout to help bring you hints, tips and advice during the 2026/27 Fantasy Premier League (FPL) season. Scout will be using their expertise to provide advice and gameweek tips which should prove useful in ensuring you win your mini-leagues. Here, we look at which of the Blues' players are must-haves, who the best value-for-money picks are, and why Joao Pedro (£7.6) is Chelsea’s most popular player. Cole Palmer (£9.5m) looked back to his best and delivered a differential 13-point haul for his 14% ownership. The Englishman added a second-half goal to his assist in the first minute on his way to securing maximum bonus points. Palmer was involved in everything going forward, racking up five shots and three chances created. His performance against Fulham will encourage Fantasy managers - Cole returned 244 points in 29 starts during the 2023/24 season, especially with other premium assets blanking on the opening weekend. The Blues’ two summer signings, Morgan Rogers (£7.5m) and Maxence Lacroix (£6.0m), have put themselves firmly on Fantasy managers’ radars. The former continued where he left off in Chelsea’s final pre-season friendly against Real Sociedad by scoring one of three shots he had at Craven Cottage. Rogers’ goal was assisted by Lacroix, who topped off a superb defensive display with an impressive assist, showcasing his offensive threat. The Frenchman also returned defensive contribution points, something he made a habit of doing last season in a Crystal Palace shirt. Unsurprisingly, Joao Pedro (£7.6m) is the highest-owned Chelsea player in FPL. The Brazilian currently sits in 67% of teams, second among all players. Over 290,000 managers have transferred in the Brazilian ahead of Friday’s GW2 deadline, resulting in a price rise of £0.1m, following his 11-point haul against Fulham. Joao Pedro, who was the only forward to score more than nine points in GW1, picked up a goal, an assist and claimed a share of the bonus points. Last season, the Brazilian returned 177 Fantasy points thanks to 15 goals and nine assists, his best-ever season across all three metrics. The underlying data for Joao Pedro in 2025/26 was equally impressive. No Chelsea player managed more shots (73), big chances (26) or Expected Goals (14.96). JP will be keen to impress against his old club Brighton on Sunday. The Seagulls are in UEFA Conference League action on Thursday. In defence, Josh Acheampong (£4.5m) played the full 90 minutes and returned defensive contribution points. No Chelsea player racked up more DefCons than the Englishman’s tally of 15, thanks to five tackles, seven clearances, two blocks and one interception. Acheampong is attractively priced if he can keep his place with Wesley Fofana (£5.0m) returning from suspension. On the other side of the back-three, Levi Colwill (£5.0m) also featured. The Englishman scored against his former club Brighton at Stamford Bridge back in the 2023/24 season. Bruno Fernandes (£12.0m) is likely to be the most captained player this weekend for Manchester United’s home match against Ipswich Town. Despite a disappointing result in Gameweek 1, the Red Devils’ captain registered three shots and three chances created against Hull. With penalties and other set-pieces in his locker, Fernandes carries explosive potential for Gameweek 2. Elsewhere, Erling Haaland (£15.5m) will be looking to get off the mark against Crystal Palace on Friday night after blanking on the opening weekend. Last season’s Golden Boot winner racked up 239 points in 25/26 thanks to 27 goals, eight assists and 43 bonus points. The Norwegian’s underlying numbers were encouraging against Bournemouth, with a match-high five shots and a 0.74 xG tally.

news.title: Training ahead of Brighton ☀️
National League Cup report: Wycombe Wanderers Women 0-6 Chelsea Women's Under-18s
news.body_en: Chelsea Women’s Under-18s made a superb start to their senior Women’s National League Cup campaign with a commanding 6-0 victory away at Wycombe Wanderers Women Chelsea N'Drin opened the scoring from the penalty spot on the half-hour and the Blues then struck five times after the interval, as Tess Finn, N'Drin again, Carla Gardiner, Maisie Brickell and Rebekah Pierce also found the net. Leanne Champ's side created a host of chances and dealt impressively with the physicality of their senior opponents, combining sharp transition play with composed finishing while keeping a clean sheet. Chelsea were made to work for the opening goal by a physical Wycombe side, but our youngsters continued to create chances and our positive play down the right was rewarded after 30 minutes. Gabi Storey, Keira Johnson and Brickell combined before the latter drove into the penalty area. Brickell skipped beyond three Wycombe players and was eventually brought down, leaving the referee to point to the spot. N'Drin stepped up and converted with power and placement into the corner, giving Chelsea a deserved lead that we carried into the interval. The Blues resumed with real purpose and doubled the advantage two minutes into the second half. Storey and Johnson combined on the right, with the latter delivering a low cross into the area. N'Drin's first effort was blocked, but Jahyma Putman recovered possession and spun before finding Finn on the edge of the box. The midfielder drove forward and finished across goal. Chelsea's reaction to a Wycombe throw-in brought the third goal on 57 minutes. Brickell won the first contact high up the pitch and Johnson controlled the ball before turning and releasing N'Drin on the right side of the area. The forward spotted the goalkeeper advancing from her line and produced a composed chip to claim her second goal. Gardiner was introduced in place of N'Drin after 65 minutes and needed only one minute to make an impact. Patient build-up play was recycled to goalkeeper Freya Weeks, whose long diagonal pass cleared the Wycombe defence and found Putman. Her early cross was met first time by the arriving Gardiner to make it 4-0. Chelsea added a fifth on 81 minutes after reacting quickly to regain possession in the middle third. Gardiner found Pierce on the left and the substitute drove inside before playing through Wycombe's defensive line for Brickell, who supplied a composed finish. There was still time for one final goal in the second minute of stoppage time. Chelsea won the first and second balls from a long Wycombe goal-kick, allowing captain Belle Sullivan to combine with Finn in midfield. Finn passed into Pierce's forward run and the substitute advanced into space before sending a superb long-range finish dipping beneath the crossbar. The emphatic victory puts Chelsea at the top of Group D after the opening round of Women's National League Cup fixtures, with two group matches remaining. Chelsea return to Professional Game Academy South League action on Sunday 30 August, when Crystal Palace visit. Chelsea Women Under-18s (4-3-3): Freya Weeks; Elise Christian, Sophie Leach, Gabi Storey (Sadie Gregory 72’), Zoe Ciccardini; Belle Sullivan (c), Tess Finn, Keira Johnson; Jahyma Putman (Rebekah Pierce 72’), Chelsea N'Drin (Carla Gardiner 65’), Maisie BrickellUnused subs: Bella BartlettScorers: N'Drin 30 (pen), 57; Finn 47; Gardiner 66; Brickell 81; Pierce 90+2Manager: Leanne Champ

news.title: Jorja Fox leaves Chelsea
news.body_en: Chelsea can confirm defender Jorja Fox has today completed a permanent move to Ipswich Town. Fox joined the Chelsea Academy at the age of eight and made her senior debut for the Blues in a 4-0 away victory against Aston Villa in the 2020/21 campaign. Later that season, she made her first start in a 5-0 win over London City Lionesses. Her first professional contract with the club came in August 2021, on the day she turned 18. Loans to Charlton Athletic, Brighton and Hove Albion and Crystal Palace followed as she gained experience at senior level. Fox signed a contract extension with Chelsea in August 2024 and last season joined Newcastle United on a further loan. On the international stage, Fox represented England at every youth level during her time with the Blues. Everyone at Chelsea would like to wish Jorja every success in her future career.

news.title: Important information on Stamford Bridge bag policy
news.body_en: Ahead of Chelsea's first Premier League home match of the 2026/27 season, we would like to remind supporters of the bag policy in place at Stamford Bridge. The Terrorism (Protection of Premises) Act 2025, also known as ‘Martyn’s Law’, will come into effect in the UK in 2027. The legislation will require the club to demonstrate enhanced and robust security arrangements for everyone attending our home games. The bag policy is one of the measures we have in place for the safety and security of everyone attending our matches. To help maintain a safe environment and support quicker entry to Stamford Bridge, only bags no larger than A4 size are permitted. The maximum permitted dimensions are 30cm × 20cm × 10cm, approximately the size of a standard handbag. In anticipation of the requirements under Martyn’s Law, the bag policy will be strictly applied for all home matchdays at Stamford Bridge. Any bag that exceeds these dimensions will not be permitted into the stadium. The club strongly recommends that supporters avoid bringing bags to Stamford Bridge where possible. Supporters bringing a permitted bag should allow extra time for entry, as all bags are subject to search. While the club does not provide a bag storage facility at the stadium, options are available in the local area, including a matchday bag drop provided by Fulham Broadway Shopping Centre. You can find more information about this bag drop by clicking here. Any bag storage services in the local area are operated independently and are not affiliated with or controlled by the club. Exemptions to bag size restrictions will continue to be available for supporters who need to bring accessibility or medical equipment. More information on requesting a medical exemption can be found by clicking this link.

news.title: Caleb Wiley seals loan switch
news.body_en: Chelsea defender Caleb Wiley has completed a season-long loan move to Championship club Preston North End. The USA international joined the Blues from MLS side Atlanta United in July 2024 after representing his country at that summer’s Olympic Games. The 21-year-old has previously spent time on loan at RC Strasbourg in France and had two spells with Watford in the second tier. We look forward to monitoring and supporting Caleb throughout his loan at Deepdale.

news.title: Alonso Press Conference 🎙️
Xabi Alonso confirms Chelsea team news for Brighton visit
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso is hopeful Chelsea midfielder Moises Caicedo will be ready to face Brighton & Hove Albion on Sunday, and says Levi Colwill and Geovany Quenda are in contention to face the Seagulls. Our third game of the week comes in the Premier League, as we welcome Fabian Hurzeler's side to Stamford Bridge. It is an opportunity for the Blues to make it three wins from three matches at the start of the campaign. Our latest victory came on Thursday evening as we defeated Luton Town in the Carabao Cup second round. Alonso selected a strong side, with a Danny Welbeck header and an own goal from Hakeem Odoffin sealing our progression to the third round. Neither Colwill nor Quenda were involved against the Hatters. Yet Alonso stressed there was no reason for concern, with both players being managed through a busy week. He explained: ‘There were no issues, and the plan is that they are training [from Friday] and preparing for the game on Sunday. 'With Levi, after his injury last season, he is still in a period where he has to take the right steps, we don’t want to push him too much. We want to make sure [his body] doesn't get stressed and that he feels comfortable and well. It’s the same with Geo as well.’ Caicedo hasn't yet featured for the Blues this season due to what, ahead of our opening fixture, Alonso detailed as a setback suffered in training. However, the Blues boss is hopeful the Ecuadorian will train ahead of the visit of his former club and be available for selection come Sunday's game. Alonso said: ‘He is hopefully training [on Friday] and we are hopeful that he can be involved [against Brighton]. But we need to check. No decision has been made.’ One player expected to be in contention to return for the Blues on Sunday is Wesley Fofana, who served the second of his two-match suspension against Luton. Summer signing Jordan Henderson, meanwhile, may need more time, with Alonso confirming in his pre-match press conference that the Blues are waiting for him to be given the 'green light to play soon' following the injury he sustained during the World Cup.

news.title: Analysis: How POTM Estevao provided Chelsea’s spark
news.body_en: We take a detailed look at Estevao Willian’s role in Chelsea’s Carabao Cup victory over Luton Town after he was voted as our Player of the Match by the Blues supporters. The Blues booked our place in the third round of this season’s Carabao Cup – where we will take on old rivals Leeds United – by defeating Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge on Thursday evening. Estevao played a key role in our victory. The Brazil international had a hand in both our goals and earned 34 per cent of votes in our Player of the Match ballot on the Chelsea Official App. Here's why... Having come off the bench in our Premier League opener away at Fulham, Estevao was handed his chance to impress new manager Xabi Alonso from the start in our first home game of 2026/27. That came as Alonso shifted to a 4-2-3-1 shape for his starting line-up – and it is a system that suits the Brazilian winger well. Operating on the right, Estevao was able to drift inside onto his left foot. Along with Morgan Rogers doing the same on the opposite flank, the two wide men were able to link up with Cole Palmer and striker Danny Welbeck ahead of him to overload Luton’s defence in the centre of the pitch. Estevao’s movement from that right-wing also created space for the marauding Malo Gusto to use his pace to overlap into promising crossing positions and create chances. It was that which led to Chelsea’s opening goal shortly after half-time, when Estevao and Gusto combined well to give the Frenchman the chance to deliver a dangerous cross from wide, headed in by Welbeck to give the striker his first goal for the club. Chelsea dominated the ball against our League One opponents; clear from our 65.7 per cent share of possession on the night. It allowed us to take the game to Luton and play high up the pitch, giving Estevao ample opportunity to operate where he does best, causing problems deep into opposition territory. As always, the Brazilian’s ability when running with the ball was a big part of that. His five dribbles were the most of any player on the pitch and he successfully completed four of them, also the highest number of the game. He had the end product to make those dribbles count too, with his six crosses the most of any player and five chances created, the joint-best alongside Palmer. Palmer was also the only player to register more than Estevao’s four shots across the 90 minutes, and it was one of those by the latter which made our victory safe, when the Brazilian’s low drive was deflected in off Luton defender Hakeem Odoffin, officially being recorded as an own goal.

news.title: Chelsea Football Club announces Circle Internet Group as Principal Partner
news.body_en: Chelsea Football Club today announces a landmark partnership with Circle Internet Group, Inc, one of the world’s leading internet financial platform companies. The new partnership sees Circle become a Principal Partner and our official front-of-shirt partner beginning with the 2026/27 season. The partnership comes at a pivotal moment for the world. Stablecoins are moving from early adoption toward the mainstream, creating an unprecedented opportunity to make money as open, accessible, and useful as the internet itself. By reducing the cost and friction of moving value, they can broaden participation in the global economy and unlock greater opportunity for people everywhere. Bringing USDC to one of sport’s biggest global stages reflects the scale and ambition of this opportunity. Founded in 2013, Circle is a pioneer in digital assets and is helping build the financial system for the internet. At its centre is USDC, the world’s leading regulated stablecoin. USDC is a trusted digital dollar that enables people and businesses to move money globally with internet speed and 24/7 availability. In the 2026/27 season, Circle and USDC brands will appear on the front of Chelsea's Men's, Women's and Academy shirts, featuring for the first time at Chelsea FC men’s first Premier League home game of the season this Sunday against Brighton. Jeremy Allaire, Co-Founder and CEO, Circle: 'We built USDC on the belief that money should work seamlessly for everyone everywhere, the way the internet does. Partnering with Chelsea connects us with a global sports community built on that exact same borderless vision. Kash Razzaghi, Chief Commercial Officer, Circle: 'This partnership represents a shared belief in where the world is headed. Chelsea connects hundreds of millions of people across every border, and USDC is digital money that moves across those same borders. USDC on the iconic Chelsea shirt shows the world what the future of global finance looks like: open, borderless, and built for everyone. Jason Gannon, President, Chelsea FC: 'This partnership with Circle positions Chelsea at the forefront of football’s digital evolution. We are two organisations fixated by the future and are relentlessly innovating to be in the best position possible for the long-term. We look forward to beginning our journey with Circle – to introduce Circle to the Chelsea family and continue enhancing how we operate' Aki Mandhar, CEO, Chelsea FC Women: ‘We are excited to introduce Circle and USDC to the Chelsea Women family for our inaugural season at Stamford Bridge. Forging and facilitating connections between people is what Chelsea Women and Circle do best and we look forward to bringing USDC to the CFCW fanbase and beyond.’ Todd Kline, President of Commercial, Chelsea FC: ‘Circle is changing how money moves around the world, and we’re changing what it means to be a global football club. That’s real alignment, not just in values but in our shared ambition to lead on a global stage. This is more than a logo on a shirt, it represents a partner who’s building something. We’re excited to see what we can build together.’ Don't miss out! Click here to register your interest and be the first to know when our newly branded 2026/27 home and away shirts go on sale!

news.title: Mamadou Sarr completes loan switch
news.body_en: Mamadou Sarr has completed a season-long loan move to Real Sociedad. The defender has made seven appearances for Chelsea since joining from Strasbourg last summer, including one in our triumphant FIFA Club World Cup campaign. Earlier this year, Sarr started for Senegal as they defeated Morocco 1-0 in the Africa Cup of Nations final. He was also involved in their squad for this summer's FIFA World Cup. We wish Mamadou well in the Basque Country and look forward to monitoring his progress throughout the season.

news.title: Alonso on a 'special day' for Blues debutants and why Palmer played 90
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso believes our Carabao Cup victory over Luton Town was a ‘special day’ that Blues debutants Valentin Barco, Mike Penders and Danny Welbeck will long remember. Having not featured in our opening fixture of the season away to Fulham on Monday night, the trio were named in the Chelsea starting XI by Alonso for our first outing of the campaign at Stamford Bridge. All made their mark on the contest. Welbeck scored our opener against the Hatters with a well-taken header from a Malo Gusto cross. Barco was involved in our second goal of the night, winning the ball in midfield before finding Cole Palmer, who put Estevao Willian in a position to force an own goal from Hakeem Odoffin At the opposite end, Penders wasn’t unduly tested by Luton but ended his Chelsea debut with a deserved clean sheet. Alonso was pleased for each of the trio, as well as those who were making their full debuts or first competitive outings at Stamford Bridge. He said: 'For them it's a special day that they will remember. Mike will be happy because for a goalkeeper, to make his debut and keep a clean sheet feels good. Valentin had an impressive performance: very dynamic, good with the ball, very aware of what was going on in the midfield. ‘Danny was the patient player. He was the one who had to be in the box waiting for one good cross to come. In the first half we were close but we couldn’t get it. ‘Then he scored the first goal, which was important. A great cross from Malo and he did what he does best: to be in the right place and score.’ Our debuting trio were part of a strong side named by Alonso. Among the starters was Cole Palmer, who completed 90 minutes and ended the game with the captain’s armband after Reece James was brought off in the second period. Alonso was asked after the game why he felt Palmer was ready to start and finish the contest against the Hatters. He replied: 'Cole has had a great pre-season and is well prepared, so he’s one of the players who can take the 90 minutes. 'We had an idea, depending on the context of the game, but Cole has a very good fitness level in terms of his stamina and now he needs to recover well on Sunday.'

news.title: From the archive: Azpilicueta's ingenuity helps Chelsea complete the set
news.body_en: Chelsea legend Cesar Azpilicueta turns 37 today, and to celebrate our former skipper's birthday, we tell the story of the vital role he played when we first won it all. Azpilicueta served Chelsea with distinction between 2012 and 2023, and in his penultimate season at the club, became the first player in our history to win every major trophy possible The last piece of silverware required was what was then known as the Club World Cup, and has since been rebranded as the Intercontinental Cup following the expansion of the tournament we won this summer. In February 2022, we beat Al Hilal in the semi-final, setting up a showdown with Brazilian side Palmeiras. It was there, in the heat of Abu Dhabi, that our skipper's ingenuity helped ensure we returned home with a new piece of silverware in tow. It looked like the final was heading to penalties, but a shot from the Spaniard was blocked by a hand. VAR came into play, not for the first time at the Mohammed Zayed Stadium, and a spot-kick was awarded to the Blues. Azpilicueta immediately gathered the ball, and it very much looked like he was going to take the penalty in the absence of Jorginho, our regular taker. ‘It was a tactic because I knew how they are, I knew they were coming for the penalty taker, so I took the ball,’ said Azpilicueta, clearly a step ahead of everyone else in the stadium. ‘Kai [Havertz] knew that he was going to shoot, so it was to release the pressure from him. It was a decisive moment, and Kai is one of the best penalty takers. ‘I waited and listened to everything their players told me, and I think it worked, which is the most important thing.’ How it worked! Havertz coolly converted from 12 yards, and we saw out the closing stages with the minimum of fuss to secure our second trophy of that campaign, and the ninth of Azpilicueta's Blues career. For our dependable Spaniard, it marked a completion of the set, and redemption for defeat to Corinthians nearly a decade prior. ‘I’m really proud of it,’ the skipper beamed after the game. ‘We have come a long way to be here. It’s a moment to be proud and enjoy it because we know how difficult it is to win this trophy. 2012 hurt a lot and we took more than nine years to be back. We missed out in 2012 and we didn’t want to miss the cup again. ‘This time the medal is gold, and the other one is silver. I made sure I wasn’t coming back with the same colour of medal. It was a difficult game. World champions, it’s not easy. We showed the team we are. ‘When I arrived in 2012, I couldn’t imagine the journey I would go on,’ added Azpi. ‘I’m really proud to be the Chelsea captain leading the club on and off the pitch. This title feels very good because it’s the first time in our history. I’m so proud we achieved it.’ After joining Chelsea from Marseille in the summer of 2012 as a full-back little known on these shores, Azpilicueta went on to win the Premier League twice, the Champions League, the Europa League twice, the FA Cup, the League Cup, the Super Cup and, after two hours of tense football in the UAE, the Club World Cup. No Chelsea player can lay claim to such a varied honours' board. His place in the pantheon of Blues greats is secured.

news.title: Welbeck: 'It's such a privilege to play with these players'
news.body_en: Danny Welbeck has described playing with his Chelsea team-mates as ‘such a privilege’ and believes the Blues can achieve ‘something special’ over the coming years. Welbeck marked his Chelsea debut against Luton with a goal as the Blues reached the third round of the League Cup courtesy of our 2-0 victory at Stamford Bridge. The 35-year-old’s career has seen him represent England 42 times, win the title at Manchester United and lift the FA Cup twice during his time at Arsenal. He has played with some of the Premier League’s greatest ever players over the years but still appreciates being able to share a pitch with the likes of Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Estevao Willian. 'It's such a privilege to play with some of these players and it's a joy when you're out there on the pitch,’ he said. ‘For me, playing as a nine today, it was more about staying on the last line. When the ball came into me, I was always ready to link up with the likes of Morgan and Cole. I really enjoyed that and I'm looking forward to it happening a lot more.' This summer has seen the Blues sign experienced players like Welbeck, Jordan Henderson and Maxence Lacroix, while continuing to add exciting talents such as Valentin Barco, Geovany Quenda and Marco Palestra to our squad. With world-class operators like Moises Caicedo, Reece James and Palmer already among our ranks, plus the addition of a title-winning manager in Xabi Alonso, Welbeck believes the Blues could have a season to remember. 'We can build something special here,’ he said. 'With the quality of players we have here, it's only right that we believe we can achieve something special. We'll keep pushing and working every single day, and we'll be trying to get those results at the weekends.' Welbeck signed for the Blues on August 1 from Brighton and Hove Albion, and started two games during our pre-season tour, before injury ruled him out of our season opener against Fulham on Monday night. He returned on Thursday night to make his competitive debut and had an immediate impact, linking up well with the likes of Estevao, Palmer and Rogers as the Blues laid siege to Luton’s goal. It was the striker who finally broke the deadlock early in the second half when he headed in Malo Gusto’s superb first-time cross. Welbeck said: 'It's really nice to get a goal on your debut and to get off the mark right from the start. So I am really pleased with that. 'More importantly, I'm pleased to get through to the next round and we've got to stand strong in every single competition this season.' The Blues had 26 shots on the night but had to remain patient as they searched for the opener, with Welbeck concluding: 'I think patience was really important. It's never easy against a low block, so you have to keep circulating the ball, moving it from side to side and looking for openings. 'In the first half, there were a few opportunities where we could maybe have got the first goal, but it didn't quite come. At half-time, the message was to get the ball into the box a bit earlier and put some crosses in. 'It was a good message and it worked well. Malo put in a quality delivery and I was there to nod it in.' Blues fans will be hoping this was the first of many for Danny this season.

news.title: Full Match: Chelsea vs Luton Town
Extended: Chelsea 2-0 Luton Town
Xabi Alonso on conviction, patience and learning from Luton victory
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso accepts Luton Town made it difficult for his Chelsea side to secure a place in the Carabao Cup third round, but feels the Blues gained valuable experience by breaking down a low block during tonight's 2-0 victory at Stamford Bridge. Alonso's side had to work hard during our first competitive home outing of the season. The Hatters sat deep and in a compact shape; it was not an easy evening. That was reflected in the fact that the game was goalless at half-time. However, five minutes into the second period, we broke the deadlock as a wonderful cross from Malo Gusto was headed home by Danny Welbeck on his Chelsea debut. Victory was secured as the game moved toward its conclusion. Estevao Willian played a key role in the goal, driving a shot toward the far corner that defender Hakeem Odoffin could only turn into his own net. Our win – and the manner of it - was vindication for the strength of the starting XI named by Alonso. He was not taking the Hatters lightly. 'We always want to choose a competitive team, he said. 'We are taking all the games seriously, and we are in a moment in the season where many things and processes are starting. 'I’m happy many players had their first minutes for the club, making their debut and playing their first competitive game in this stadium. It wasn’t easy - credit to Luton, as they made it difficult – but we played with conviction and patience, knowing the first goal was going to come in a moment, and Danny took it really well.' The post-match stats highlighted our dominance across the 90 minutes. We enjoyed 65 per cent possession, registered 26 shots, 45 touches in the opposition area and limited Luton to just one shot on target. It's why Alonso again described his side's display as 'serious' and emphasised how the game could prove beneficial for the Blues during the season ahead. 'For sure, it’s a performance to learn how to attack a low block. Against a 5-4-1, it’s not easy against any team from any league. We need to learn from today, as we will face this context in other games as well.'

news.title: Highlights: Chelsea 2-0 Luton Town
Alonso on Carabao Cup win 🎤
Welbeck reacts to debut goal
Match report: Chelsea 2-0 Luton Town
news.body_en: Danny Welbeck's debut header and an own goal from Hakeem Odoffin ensured the Blues booked a place in the Carabao Cup third round after overcoming Luton Town 2-0 at Stamford Bridge. Xabi Alonso, overseeing a competitive game in the Stamford Bridge dugout for the first time, named a strong side and the Blues controlled the contest from start to finish. However, the game was goalless at the interval despite several chances being fashioned. The deadlock was broken early into the second period – and it was a well-constructed goal. Estevao Willian linked up with Malo Gusto down the right flank, before the France international produced an inch-perfect cross for Welbeck to head home. Estevao was a constant threat and, with 11 minutes remaining, the Brazilian forced our second as his low drive struck the unfortunate Odoffin on its route to goal. We could have had more goals – Cole Palmer was denied on several occasions and both Morgan Rogers and Jamie Gittens hit the woodwork – but importantly the Blues have advanced to set up a third-round tie with Leeds United. Alonso included three debutants in his starting XI: Mike Penders, Valentin Barco and Danny Welbeck. They came into a strong side that also included Malo Gusto, Josh Acheampong, Maxence Lacroix, Pep Chavarria, Reece James, Estevao, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer. The game quickly settled into a pattern, with the Blues probing a resolute and deep Luton backline. Space was tight, but we carved our way through on multiple occasions. Palmer was first to threaten. The England international deftly exchanged passes with Estevao on the edge of the Luton area and whipped a shot toward goal. Josh Keeley saved and quickly reacted to deny Palmer on the rebound. From the resultant corner, Palmer dragged a shot wide. Gusto then fired a shot comfortably over the crossbar as we searched for the opener. Keeley was worked again midway through the half as, after Estevao had been fouled, James forced the Luton goalkeeper into a full-length save to keep out a free-kick. Our Brazilian winger then went close himself, driving a shot wide after a neat through pass from Barco. The visitors' threat was minimal during the opening 45 minutes; a header from Hakeem Odoffin that Penders easily saved was their best effort on goal. As the half moved toward its conclusion, we came inches away from breaking the deadlock. Estevao was once again involved as he broke beyond the Luton backline and cut a pass back to Rogers, who steered a volley against the crossbar. Rogers was involved in the construction of our next chance, showcasing neat footwork to evade two challenges and open up the pitch for Chavarria. The Spaniard played a pass to Palmer, but the striker's shot was blocked en route to goal. Come the half-time whistle, the Blues still had work to do. Alonso opted against any alterations at the interval – and the Blues boss was rewarded as his side opened the scoring five minutes into the second period. It was a well-crafted goal. The ball was worked to Estevao down the right flank, and the Brazil international stayed patient until the opportunity arrived to slip a pass through to the overlapping Gusto. He produced an excellent cross and Welbeck was perfectly positioned to head home. Luton attempted to rally, but they were largely kept at bay. The closest the visitors came to breaching Penders' goal were shots from distance from substitute Isaish Jones and Chelsea Academy graduate Kasey Palmer. Neither were on target, though. At the opposite end, Palmer's quest for a goal continued and our No.10 came inches away from finding the top corner with a powerful, curled attempt that flew just wide. Alonso turned to his bench with 23 minutes remaining; Jorrel Hato, Romeo Lavia and Pedro Neto were introduced for Gusto, James and Rogers. Joao Pedro replaced Joao Pedro soon after. The changes gave the Blues fresh impetus – and a second goal soon arrived to ensure our passage into the third round. Barco was instrumental, reclaiming possession in midfield and moving the ball to Palmer. He fed Estevao, who produced a quick stepover to shift the ball onto his right foot and drill a shot toward the far corner. His attempt struck Odoffin on its way to goal and ended the net. It proved Estevao's last involvement; he was replaced by Jamie Gittens before play restarted. The game was won, but there was time to add to the scoreline. Palmer continued to push for a goal and, as the game entered stoppage time, Keeley denied him once more and then stopped Joao Pedro's rebound. Gittens then went even closer, beating the Luton stopper but seeing his low drive strike the post. The third goal didn't arrive, but it didn't change the outcome. The Blues were through and, up next in the competition, come an old foe in Leeds United. The Blues go in search of our third victory in a week as we welcome Brighton and Hove Albion to Stamford Bridge on Sunday. The Premier League fixture kicks off at 2pm (UK time). Chelsea: Penders: Gusto (Hato 67), Acheampong, Lacroix, Chavarria; James (c) (Lavia 67), Barco; Estevao (Gittens 80), Palmer, Rogers (Neto 67); Welbeck (Joao Pedro 73)Chelsea substitutes: Sanchez, Anselmino, Watson, EmeghaGoalscorers: Welbeck 50, Odoffin og 79 Luton Town: Keeley, Ashby, Odoffin, Johnston, Johnson, Benagr, Walsh, Palmer, Lawrence (Fox 61), Kodua (Richards 46), MarshallLuton Town substitutes: Shea, Naismith, Andersen, Wells, Jones, Chigozle, Cole  Booked: Johnson 56

news.title: Xabi Alonso on Blues debutants and a serious approach
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso says his Chelsea side for tonight’s Carabao Cup second-round tie against Luton Town, which includes three debutants, indicates how seriously the Blues are taking the competition. Our first outing in this season's competition comes at Stamford Bridge, as we welcome the Hatters to west London. Alonso has made five changes to the side that defeated Fulham on Monday evening, but the likes of Maxence Lacroix, Reece James, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers have all been named in the starting XI. 'We want to have a good start in the Carabao Cup after the Premier League,' explained the Blues boss. 'For sure, playing at home, it needs to feel good and hopefully it will be a good start here this season. 'We want to take all the competitions seriously – for sure, this season all of them are a target. For each game, we choose the best competitive team we think and this one is good enough to go through.' Penders, who was part of our squad at last summer's Club World Cup before spending the 2025/26 campaign on loan at Strasbourg, is handed his maiden outing for the Blues. And Alonso has enjoyed working with the 21-year-old Belgian so far. He said: 'We want that he enjoys [himself], that he has composure and maturity, that he gets used to playing in a new stadium with new team-mates. 'So far, he is very mature for his age – it was great that he played very competitive football last year in Strasbourg. Now this is the next step, and we need to help him.'

news.title: Matchday Unseen | Real Sociedad 🎥
Malo Gusto on fresh objectives and wing-back requirements
news.body_en: Malo Gusto is one member of the Chelsea squad with experience of playing in a system that utilises wing-backs, so the Frenchman knows exactly what is required of the role. Gusto lined up at right wing-back in our opening-day success away to Fulham, where it was quickly apparent how important those positions will be under Xabi Alonso. If you look at our first goal, scored in rapid time, Gusto is tracking the run from deep of a Fulham attacker when we recover possession. For our second, he is much higher up the pitch and plays the pass to Palmer that instigates the attack, with Fulham’s left side out of position as Antonee Robinson is forced to track Gusto’s movement. ‘It’s a position that I used to play before at Lyon when I was young,’ Gusto tells us. ‘So I know it and I do enjoy it. You need to bring a lot of energy – make a lot of runs forward and be there to defend as well. ‘You have to try to perform to your best on both sides of the games and it’s a good system for sure, but of course as a team we have to be prepared for anything.’ Gusto says he has enjoyed his time working with Alonso and there is great respect within the group for his achievements as a player and a manager. He has noted the ‘clear plan’ Alonso has in mind for his Blues team. On a personal level, Gusto benefitted from the break following the World Cup, where he helped France to a fourth-placed finish. Now, with three points already in the bank and with home games against Luton and Brighton ahead, Gusto is excited about the prospect of being involved in a special campaign at the Bridge. ‘It was good for the body to rest and I’m feeling really good now. I couldn’t wait to come back to Chelsea and just focus on our new objectives. ‘As a Chelsea player, of course we want to compete for the title and come back to the Champions League next season. ‘We have a lot of objectives and to achieve them we need to create a good dynamic as a team and see how it goes.’

news.title: Ellie Carpenter: Sociedad second-half display 'a hint of what's to come' from Chelsea
news.body_en: Chelsea kicked off the new season with a 5-2 win against Real Sociedad in the first leg of our Women’s Champions League qualifying tie, and with two assists to her name, Ellie Carpenter was one of the star performers on the night. The Blues went in level at the interval after Ainhoa Mari had put the visitors ahead with a stunning strike before Naomi Girma equalised. A powerful header from Veerle Buurman put us in front after the break, but Sociedad fought back with a determined equaliser, and it was at that point that Chelsea had to show what we were made of. Substitute Melvine Malard scored twice on her debut, and Lauren James chipped in with another in the final stages of the match to give us a three-goal cushion heading into the second leg. After the victory, Carpenter shed light on how we clicked into gear. ‘It is quite hard going straight into such a big, important game,’ said the wing-back. ‘Some of us are not really used to that. It was a good test for us, and obviously in the first half we were a bit rusty, and we had to fix things up; we really had to get into the game. ‘We came out in the second half and really gave it to them, playing with strength and confidence as well. It was a great team performance all round. ‘It’s also good to have these big games early on in the season. It gets us ready for the WSL, which starts next weekend. We have so many amazing individual players that can play in different positions. There's so much versatility in this team. We can play different formations. So that's also a strength of ours. Get your tickets now to welcome our stars home to Stamford Bridge on 5 September! ‘The opponent doesn't really know what's coming if we keep changing, but I think our fluidity, you could see, was slowly building. We're slowly building those connections, and it's only the first game of this season. ‘Our aim was to come out strong and score plenty of goals if we could. I think we did that as a team. We played the game, and it was fun doing it. I think it was a great performance and a hint of what's to come from this team.’ Sonia Bompastor was subject to a touchline suspension for Wednesday’s match. With the head coach absent, assistant Camille Abily presided over the 5-2 victory. Our Spanish opponents were well-organised throughout the first half, but the stand-in boss worked with the team on some tactical tweaks to iron out any issues. ‘I think at half-time it was just a case of keep doing our stuff, playing fast, playing with some discipline, and then it will come,' said Carpenter. 'The coach fixed a couple of things, and we did that, and we could see the results in the second half. We pushed them and got the win. ‘One of the messages at half-time was to hold our runs a bit more and make those forward runs connecting with the passes and the player, and just waiting for the right timing. We tidied that up in the second half and really exploited their high line. ‘It was a case of getting back on top and keep doing our jobs. We'll look at those goals we conceded and how we can tighten it for the next game next week.’ Having provided the cross for Malard’s second goal, Carpenter paid tribute to our summer acquisition. The pair have reunited after playing together under Bompastor and Abily at Lyon, and they linked up straight away. ‘Obviously we have that relationship from Lyon,’ the Australian smiled. ‘So it's nice to have her on the team. She brings such great energy and such a good vibe, and she’s an amazing footballer, so I like combining with her.’ Wednesday’s match took place at Plough Lane in Wimbledon, a ground that will play host to our Women’s FA Cup matches and any league phase games we face in the Women’s Champions League. All Women’s Super League fixtures will be played at Stamford Bridge, starting with a clash against Aston Villa on Saturday 5 September. Carpenter was impressed with our second new home and paid tribute to the support from the fans in the stands. ‘It's a really nice stadium, and it's a real football stadium,’ she remarked. ‘The seats are really close. You can feel the fans. They were really pushing us throughout the whole game. We're happy to move in here.’ See Ellie Carpenter and the rest of the CFCW stars at our new Stamford Bridge home when we take on Aston Villa! Click here to secure your spot...

news.title: Chelsea vs Luton: All you need to know
news.body_en: Chelsea host Luton Town in a 7.30pm kick-off (UK time) in round two of the Carabao Cup. Club historian Rick Glanvill and club statistician Paul Dutton look ahead to the Blues' first knockout tie of 2026/27. The fixture was moved to a less familiar Thursday slot to accommodate Monday’s trip to Fulham – a 3-2 Premier League victory for the Blues. This first-ever League Cup meeting between the two clubs is the setting for new manager Xabi Alonso’s official debut in front of the Stamford Bridge faithful – travelling Chelsea supporters have already chanted his name at Craven Cottage. The Blues are the capital’s most successful contestants in the tri-handled trophy with five wins, and we most recently contested the final in 2024. Back in December, our quarter-final victory at Cardiff City made it 19 straight wins against lower-league opponents in this floodlit trophy quest. The Blues then bowed out at the semi-final stage to eventual runners-up Arsenal. Luton’s greatest moment of giant-killing came in defeating the Gunners in the 1988 final of this competition. They last encountered top-flight opposition in the League Cup in September 2020, losing 3-0 to Manchester United – one of eight losses in the past nine encounters with top-flight opponents in this competition. Prior to beating Gillingham this month, the third-tier Hatters had been eliminated in round one of the Carabao Cup for three seasons in a row. All round-two games are broadcast live on Sky Sports platforms and this one is on Sky Sports channels 401 and 402, and their app. Wesley Fofana is suspended, while Xabi Alonso confirmed that both Moises Caicedo and Marco Palestra will miss Thursday’s Carabao Cup clash. Elsewhere, the Spaniard stated that goalkeeper Mike Penders has an opportunity to feature. ‘Let’s see, hopefully Moi could make it for the weekend, but we need to check a little bit more with Marco,' said Alonso in his pre-match press conference. ‘Otherwise everyone from Monday is okay, Cole [Palmer] is absolutely fine. Penders is part of the squad, so he has an opportunity. We will decide and then I am giving the team tomorrow to the players, so I prefer to respect that they know first.' In our history, Chelsea have exited at this stage of the competition on 13 occasions, though not since October 1995, to Stoke City over two legs. There were some memorable round-two matches in the early years of the competition, not least 3-0 away to Birmingham City on 23 September 1966, when Jim McCalliog became one of the club’s youngest debutants on his 18th birthday. The same month three years later, local visitors Charlton Athletic were thrashed 5-2 and the Blues also hit the bar four times. The clash with Sheffield Wednesday in 1970 required a replay, in which Dave Sexton’s regular ploy of throwing Dave Webb up front paid off. The utility man netted the winner for 2-1. In 1984, over two legs, John Neal’s side took what proved an unassailable 3-1 lead to Millwall’s Den, Kerry Dixon levelling in a 1-1 draw. We went on to reach the semi-finals. A shock 1-0 first leg-loss at York City was thankfully overturned 3-0 at the Bridge in 1986. The Londoners had a reputation for embarrassing defeats by lower league sides and rarely did that jinx hurt more than a 3-1 second-leg loss at Tranmere Rovers in 1991. A 5-4 aggregate victory over Blackpool in 1996 would prove our last round-two entry for 20 years, until a feisty Bristol Rovers outfit were edged out 3-2 on the Fulham Road, Michy Batshuayi bagging a brace. Our most recent match at the stage came in 2023, against Wimbledon. The Wombles took the lead through a penalty but succumbed 2-1 after a spot-kick in reply from Noni Madueke and an Enzo Fernandez winner into an empty net. Luton Town’s last win at the Bridge was through a penalty shootout in the little-regarded Zenith Data Systems Cup in February 1991. The Hatters’ most recent Fulham Road visit was a 3-0 Premier League loss in 2023, with Raheem Sterling (twice) and Nicolas Jackson finding the net. Chelsea are London’s most successful club in this competition, winning it five times, including the capital’s first and most recent successes.  Our ten League Cup final appearances is bettered only by Liverpool (15). Chelsea and Luton have met 47 times previously across all competitions, the Blues winning 21 of those encounters. We have prevailed in each of the past five meetings between the two on all fronts, starting with the 1994 FA Cup semi-final at Wembley. Chelsea’s record victory in this competition remains the 7-0 win at Doncaster Rovers on 16 November 1960, during our maiden League Cup campaign. Our two previous second-round appearances were also at Stamford Bridge, the 3-2 win over Bristol Rovers in 2016 and the 2-1 success against Wimbledon in 2023. Luton are playing their last few seasons at their quirky Kenilworth Road home, while a 25,000-seater stadium emerges in the town centre. Goal-line technology and VAR will not be in operation until the semi-finals, unless all host stadiums in the round are suitably equipped. Nine substitutes can be named and five used in the game (plus a concussion replacement if required). Yellow cards and suspensions apply only to this competition. Red card bans are served across all domestic fronts. Players are no longer cup tied if they move from one club to another during a transfer window. Each tie is decided on the night and extra-time is not used to decide ties until the second leg of the semi-finals.  In the event of scores being level after second-half stoppage time, the outcome will be decided by a penalty shoot-out.

news.title: Quenda on settling in England and first impressions of Chelsea
news.body_en: Geovany Quenda introduces himself to the Chelsea supporters with an exclusive interview in the programme for our first home game of the season against Luton Town in the Carabao Cup. The Portuguese winger made his competitive debut as a substitute against Fulham at Craven Cottage on Monday and tells us about his close friendship with Dario Essugo, the encouragement he has received from Xabi Alonso and the 'family' atmosphere at Cobham. 'We had a good pre-season and I think now it’s about making sure we also have a good start to the season,' he says of his first few weeks as a Blue. 'For me, I just need to help the team. That’s the most important thing – help the team to win. Of course, it’s difficult to come to another country, but this is my job.' Quenda also talks about his journey from Guinea-Bissau to the Premier League, via Sporting Lisbon, where so many other great players in his position emerged in the past couple of generations, from Luis Figo to Cristiano Ronaldo. We also delve into the distant past and uncover the long-forgotten stories of two Luton Town goal machines who swapped Kenilworth Road for Stamford Bridge either side of the Second World War. Joe Payne and Hugh Billington were two of the great goal scorers of their time, and we take a deeper look into their lives, with help from the research of Billington’s distant relative and genealogist, Kai Ridds. We also relive the 1994 FA Cup semi-final, when Chelsea legend Kerry Dixon came up against his former side with Luton Town at Wembley. Then there’s all the usual columns, news and stats, bringing you fresh insight and keeping you up to date with the latest goings on at the club. news.title: UWCL Highlights: Chelsea 5-2 Real Sociedad
Xabi Alonso says Blues duo in contention to face Luton
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has confirmed Danny Welbeck and Emmanuel Emegha could make their Chelsea debuts when we take on Luton Town in the second round of the Carabao Cup. The attacking duo didn’t feature in our final friendly, against Real Sociedad, nor our Premier League opener at Craven Cottage earlier in the week, when Welbeck was an unused substitute. Our manager had positive news on their fitness, but confirmed the game will come too soon for another new signing, Jordan Henderson. ‘Danny and Emma, yes [they will be in contention to face Luton],’ said Alonso. ‘Jordan will take a little bit longer. Let's see. I'm not a doctor and I don't have the data. We need to wait until we know more.' It is still early days for Alonso at Chelsea, but the early signs in our victory at Craven Cottage were very promising indeed. Our new manager knows there is plenty of work ahead to mould this Blues team in his image, but he is confident to see consistent progress as the campaign unfolds. 'Most of the teams will get better and better in the weeks ahead and with more games,’ said Alonso. ‘We have some players that have just been back for two weeks, they are in good shape but they will get better. 'There are teams that have been working longer with their manager and so many ideas are already very established. With other projects, in different cases, it takes more time. So there will be a development of many concepts. 'As I said in another press conference, I think that we started our season Monday and the way we will be playing in January will be different. And I think it's going to be better, and the next year will be even better.'

news.title: Chelsea learn potential Carabao Cup third round opponents
news.body_en: Should we progress past Luton Town in the Carabao Cup tomorrow, we will play at Stamford Bridge in the third round of the competition. The draw was made after Everton’s victory at Preston North End and it handed Xabi Alonso’s side a potential tie against Leeds United, who defeated Nottingham Forest in the second round. It would be our third League Cup tie against Leeds, following victories in 1969, 2001 and, most memorably, 2012, when we won 5-1 at Elland Road in the quarter-finals. Third-round ties will be split across two midweek slots to accommodate European fixture commitments, with games played on the weeks beginning 7 September and 14 September. Should we beat Luton, fixture and ticket details will follow in due course. Chelsea or Luton v Leeds United West Ham v Fulham or AFC Wimbledon

news.title: Camille Abily praises attack and gives fitness update on Naomi Girma
news.body_en: Chelsea assistant coach Camille Abily hailed our wealth of resources in attack as our new number nine Melvine Malard scored a brace on her debut in our 5-2 win over Real Sociedad at Plough Lane on Wednesday. The striker combined with former Lyon teammate Ellie Carpenter for her second of the evening, the pair having worked under Abily and head coach Sonia Bompastor at the French club in the past. ‘They know each other really well,’ said Abily, who was deputising on the touchline for the suspended Bompastor. ‘They also get on really well. They speak in French sometimes, so it helps because no one understands. ‘It would be great anytime we are able to score five goals. Of course, we have quality on the pitch, and also on the bench, because today the subs helped the team a lot. ‘Up front, we have Melvine. We have Mayra (Ramirez). She's not here yet, but I hope she will be soon. Aggie (Beever-Jones) is able to play this position. Last year, Lauren James played in this position. ‘That wasn't what we wanted, but when we are missing forwards sometimes we need it. Melvine is really versatile. She's able to play different positions and Aggie also, so it can help the team.’ Sociedad took the lead after just seven minutes, and fought back to level the scores at 2-2 before we extended our lead in the latter stages of the contest. Abily paid tribute to the opposition, and explained some of the half-time tactical tweaks she made to turn the performance around. ‘It was a tough game,’ she said. ‘Especially in the first half because Real Sociedad are a really great team, but I think we had a good reaction. We were so much better in the second half. There was also more space for us. So a tough win, but a good win. ‘At half-time we said we wanted to find and play in the spaces behind because their back line was really high. We score many goals like this, so this is sort of what we want to do, so it was good. ‘It was a good experience on the touchline. It was fun, but it's okay. Sonia can take the spot again!’ Finally, the assistant coach explained why defender Naomi Girma was replaced by Lucy Bronze in the second half. ‘It's more fitness,’ she said. ‘And also a decision because we have many good players on the bench, and we know with her calf we need to be careful. So for that, we didn’t want to take any risks.'
